---
title: "Formal Power Series & Generating Functions"
subtitle: "A 6-part, 24-chapter algebraic and combinatorial textbook for competitive programming"
---

This textbook is a self-contained, zero-forward-reference treatise on **Formal Power Series (FPS) and Generating Functions** for competitive programming (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`), paired with **6 Two-Stage Blind Topic-Group Checkpoints** (`CP-I`–`CP-VI`), a **14-Problem Multi-Perspective Synthesis Reserve** (`Syn-01`–`Syn-14`), and a **321-Problem Master Curated Archive** (`254` accepted problems across `192` chapter ladder slots, `48` blind checkpoint slots, and `14` synthesis reserve slots, plus `67` quarantined bare library templates `R-01`–`R-67`).

Every chapter is built from algebraic definitions ($K[[x]]$, $K((x))$, valuation topology $\nu(F)$, formal residues $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0}$, bivariate ring hierarchies, differential Weyl operators $K[x]\langle D \rangle$, Tellegen transposition, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$) with explicit **Diagnostic Signals**, **Reverse-Engineering Scratchpads**, **Characteristic-$p$ & Valuation-Shift Failure Modes**, and an inline **8-Problem 4-Tier Practice Ladder** (`2 Stepping Stones`, `2 Intermediate`, `2 Advanced`, `2 Mastery`).

Start with [FPS Ch 01 · The Ring $K[[x]]$, Valuation Topology & Newton Inversion](chapters/ch01-ring-convolutions-newton-inv.qmd), follow the [study plan and mastery gates](study-plan.qmd), and keep the [notation, operators, and 16 failure modes](notation.qmd) open alongside your work. For general number theory, linear algebra, probability, and sieves outside the FPS track, switch to the companion [Competitive Programming Mathematics](../math/index.qmd) textbook in the top navigation bar.

::: {.callout-important}
## Entry Contract (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

The 24-chapter curriculum is built on four explicit entry assumptions:

1. **Formal Power Series vs. Analytic Functions**: An element $F(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} f_n x^n \in K[[x]]$ is an infinite sequence $(f_0, f_1, f_2, \dots)$ over a commutative ring $K$, never an analytic function of a complex variable. Infinite sums $\sum_{k \ge 0} G_k(x)$ are governed purely by the **$x$-adic valuation** $\nu(G_k) \to \infty$ (finitely many non-zero contributions to $[x^n]$ for each fixed $n$), not radius of convergence.
2. **Ring Units vs. Field Division**: Division in $K[[x]]$ is checked locally before every step: $F(x)$ is invertible in $K[[x]]$ if and only if its constant term is a unit $[x^0]F(x) = f_0 \in K^\times$. Operators that integrate $\int x^{n-1}\,dx = x^n / n$ (`ln`, `exp`, `pow`, classical Lagrange inversion) additionally require the divided integers to be units in $K$; over a field, characteristic zero or prime characteristic $p > N$ suffices through degree $N$.
3. **Black-Box `mint` & `NTT` Primitive Contract**: In accordance with repository policy, chapters never dump boilerplate modular integer (`mint`), factorial sieve, or raw Cooley–Tukey butterfly `NTT` templates. You are assumed to have a working black-box polynomial multiplication primitive `mul(A, B)` running in $O(N \log N)$ over NTT-friendly primes such as $p = 998244353 = 119 \cdot 2^{23} + 1$.
4. **Notation & Defensive Contracts**: Keep the [Notation & Operator Reference](notation.qmd) open for the 16 Canonical Failure Modes (`#1`–`#16`) and operator contracts, and use the [Study Plan & Diagnostic Guide](study-plan.qmd) to navigate the 24 chapters, 6 Two-Stage Blind Checkpoints ([`CP-I`](checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd)–[`CP-VI`](checkpoints/cp06-part6-trees-qseries-sps-dirichlet.qmd)), [Multi-Perspective Synthesis Reserve](capstones/synthesis-reserve.qmd), and [321-Problem Master Archive](capstones/problem-archive-guide.qmd).
:::

## How Each Chapter and Checkpoint Works

1. **Motivation & Diagnostic Signals**: Each chapter opens with concrete contest statement shapes that defeat naive DP or combinatorial casework, and lists the exact algebraic recognition triggers.
2. **First-Principles Derivations & Hand-Checkable Examples**: Every central identity is derived as an explicit sequence of ring equalities or a double count, followed by a small numerical example worked by hand to degree $3$ or $4$.
3. **Algorithm Contracts & Defensive Failure Modes**: Every operator states its preconditions, exact index bounds, complexity in $\mathcal{M}(N)$, and how it breaks when valuation shifts ($\nu(F) \ge 1$) or small characteristic ($p \le N$ or $p \mid n$) occur.
4. **8-Problem 4-Tier Practice Ladder**: Two *Stepping Stones*, two *Intermediate*, two *Advanced*, and two *Mastery* problems per chapter, each with progressive hints and a complete self-contained algebraic derivation.
5. **Two-Stage Blind Checkpoints (`CP-I`–`CP-VI`)**: At the end of each Part, an 8-problem blind diagnostic assessment presents contest problems *without* chapter tags, training you to identify the right algebraic model before opening the stage-gated hints.

## Chapters & Checkpoints

### Part I · Foundations of Formal Power Series & Combinatorial Constructions (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`)

- [Ch 01 · The Ring $K[[x]]$, Valuation Topology & Newton Inversion](chapters/ch01-ring-convolutions-newton-inv.qmd): Cauchy convolution, $x$-adic valuation $\nu(F)$, unit criterion $[x^0]F \in K^\times$, quadratic Newton `inv`, valuation-shift precision loss, and min-heap product trees.
- [Ch 02 · Formal Calculus, 1D Newton Iteration & The $O(NK)$ Sparse Engine](chapters/ch02-calculus-frobenius-sparse-ode-newton.qmd): formal $D_x$ and $\int$, characteristic-$p$ Frobenius endomorphism $A(x)^p \equiv A(x^p) \pmod p$, 1D Newton `sqrt`/`ln`/`exp`/`pow`, 3-way modular reduction in $P(x)^\alpha$, and $O(NK)$ `sparse_div`/`sparse_ln`/`sparse_exp`/`sparse_pow`.
- [Ch 03 · The Unlabeled Symbolic Method: OGFs, Multisets & Partitions](chapters/ch03-mset-partitions-euler-polya.qmd): $\operatorname{SEQ}$, $\operatorname{PSET}$, $\operatorname{MSET}$ (Pólya $\exp$), Inverse Euler Transform via Möbius inversion, Ferrers conjugation, Euler's Pentagonal Number Theorem, and Burnside/Pólya cycle index enumeration.
- [Ch 04 · The Labeled Symbolic Method: EGFs, Boxed Products & Prüfer Trees](chapters/ch04-egf-set-cyc-boxed-prufer.qmd): relabeling binomial convolution, $\operatorname{SET} \mapsto \exp$, $\operatorname{CYC} \mapsto \ln(1-x)^{-1}$, Greene–Wilf Boxed Product $\widehat{C}' = \widehat{A}'\widehat{B}$, Rota's Twelvefold Way, and Prüfer degree-sequence EGFs.
- [Checkpoint I · Part I Blind Assessment (`CP-I`)](checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems testing `Ch 01`–`Ch 04` recognition without topic tags.

### Part II · Rational Sequences, Binomial Transforms, Roots of Unity & Inclusion–Exclusion (`Ch 05`–`Ch 08`)

- [Ch 05 · Rational Generating Functions $K(x)$, Bostan–Mori & Berlekamp–Massey](chapters/ch05-rational-bostan-mori-berlekamp-massey.qmd): rational series $P(x)/Q(x)$, reversal Euclidean `divmod`, Graeffe parity-splitting Bostan–Mori in $O(d \log d \log N)$, Heaviside partial fractions, and Berlekamp–Massey recurrence synthesis.
- [Ch 06 · Binomial Sums, Snake Oil, Taylor Shift & Stirling Engines](chapters/ch06-binomial-snake-oil-taylor-shift-stirling.qmd): Golden Rule of Index Alignment, Wilf's Snake Oil, Egorychev polynomial negative-exponent extraction, all 4 Stirling row/column $O(N \log N)$ engines, falling-factorial polynomials (`下降幂多项式`), Taylor shift $F(x+c)$, and the generalized $\alpha$-Euler transform.
- [Ch 07 · Point-Value Duality, Roots-of-Unity Filters, Cyclotomic Rings & Chirp-Z](chapters/ch07-roots-of-unity-cyclotomic-czt.qmd): root-of-unity modulo-$m$ filter (`单位根反演`), cyclotomic quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_p[\omega]/(\Phi_m(\omega))$ when $m \nmid (p-1)$, 3-prime Garner NTT (`MTT`), and Bluestein's binomial Chirp Z-Transform $F(ac^i)$.
- [Ch 08 · Sieve & Inclusion–Exclusion Engines: Run-Length Transfer, Rook & Goulden–Jackson](chapters/ch08-connected-component-ie-rook-goulden-jackson.qmd): bivariate Taylor shift $G(x, y-1)$, universal run-length IE $F(x) = W(x)/(1+W(x))$, harmonic sparsity of bounded runs, rook polynomials, and the Goulden–Jackson cluster overlap matrix $\mathbf{C}(x)^{-1}$.
- [Checkpoint II · Part II Blind Assessment (`CP-II`)](checkpoints/cp02-part2-rational-transforms-ie.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 08`.

### Part III · Online Convolutions, Implicit Equations, Formal Residues & Graph Species (`Ch 09`–`Ch 13`)

- [Ch 09 · Causal Recurrences: CDQ Divide-and-Conquer NTT & Online Relaxed Convolution](chapters/ch09-cdq-fft-online-relaxed-convolution.qmd): semi-online CDQ NTT, full-online self-convolution ($l > 0$ factor-of-$2$ symmetry invariant), van der Hoeven's `lowbit(q+1)` `RelaxedConvolution`, and online Dirichlet updates.
- [Ch 10 · Implicit Functional Equations, Coupled Newton Iteration & Unlabeled Otter Trees](chapters/ch10-implicit-equations-newton-unlabeled-trees-otter.qmd): implicit equations $A(x, F(x)) = 0$, Fréchet derivatives, $2 \times 2$ Jacobian Newton systems, integrating-factor differential Newton, Pólya–Euler rooted trees, and Otter's dissimilarity theorem $U(x) = T(x) - \frac{1}{2}(T(x)^2 - T(x^2))$.
- [Ch 11 · Formal Laurent Series $K((x))$, Residue Calculus, Raney's Lemma & 6-Form LIF](chapters/ch11-laurent-residues-raney-lagrange-inversion.qmd): formal residue invariance $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} A(x)\,dx = \operatorname{Res}_{u=0} A(G(u))G'(u)\,du$, Raney's cycle lemma and Łukasiewicz paths, all 6 canonical forms of Lagrange Inversion (including char-$p$-safe Derivative-Free LIF), `Elegia` coupled binomial sum linearization, and base-$p$ Frobenius LIF.
- [Ch 12 · Advanced Labeled Graph Species: Pointed Trees, Cacti, Deserts & Tutte Block-Cut Equations](chapters/ch12-cacti-deserts-block-cut-biconnected-graphs.qmd): pointing operator $\Theta = xD_x$, Husimi cacti and deserts, Tutte's pointed block-cut equation $\ln(\widehat{R}(x)/x) = \widehat{B}'(\widehat{R}(x))$, bridge-tree 2-edge-connected graphs, and reverse LIF coefficient extraction.
- [Ch 13 · Graphical Generating Functions: Eulerian, Bipartite, DAGs, SCCs & Symbolic Matrix-Tree](chapters/ch13-graphical-gf-eulerian-bipartite-dags-sccs.qmd): Eulerian and bipartite graph EGFs, Robinson–Stanley layer IE for DAGs and strongly connected digraphs, Wright's fixed-excess kernel decomposition, Kirchhoff Matrix-Tree, BEST theorem, symbolic determinants over $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{k+1})$, and $O(V^3)$ Hessenberg characteristic polynomials.
- [Checkpoint III · Part III Blind Assessment (`CP-III`)](checkpoints/cp03-part3-online-implicit-lif-graphs.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 13`.

### Part IV · Stochastic Processes, Lattice Walks, Bivariate Diagonals & The Kernel Method (`Ch 14`–`Ch 17`)

- [Ch 14 · Probability Generating Functions, Stopping Times, Renewal, Poissonization & Martingales](chapters/ch14-pgf-stopping-times-renewal-poisson-martingales.qmd): PGFs $F(z) = \mathbb{E}[z^T]$, formal Taylor shift $z = 1+t \bmod t^3$ for $0/0$ pole cancellation, renewal first-passage deconvolution, KMP border theorem (*The Singing Kingdom*), Poisson–Laplace–Borel bridge, and optional stopping martingales.
- [Ch 15 · 1D Lattice Walks: Reflection Principle, Chebyshev Strips & The Small-Root Kernel Method](chapters/ch15-1d-lattice-walks-chebyshev-kernel-method.qmd): André reflection, Kelvin alternating strip images and Chebyshev polynomials $U_h$, Laurent step ring $(K[y,y^{-1}])[[x]]$, and the 1D Bivariate Kernel Method (single small root, multiple small roots, and Vieta's large-root shortcut).
- [Ch 16 · Multivariate FPS: 5-Ring Hierarchy, 2D Bostan–Mori, Twisted Kronecker & Furstenberg Diagonals](chapters/ch16-bivariate-hierarchy-2d-bostan-mori-furstenberg.qmd): the 5-ring bivariate hierarchy, all 4 regimes of 2D Bostan–Mori (`Truncated`, `Eval-Interp`, `Kinoshita-Li`, `Frobenius`), van der Hoeven's $\chi$-graded twisted Kronecker substitution, Furstenberg's diagonal residue theorem in $K[[t]]((y))$, and Lipshitz 3D D-finite diagonals.
- [Ch 17 · Coupled Multivariate Systems: Quarter-Plane Obstinate Kernel, Good–Lagrange & MacMahon](chapters/ch17-quarter-plane-obstinate-kernel-good-lagrange-macmahon.qmd): Multivariate Good–Lagrange Inversion ($\det(I-J)$ Jacobian and bipartite rank-1 shortcut), MacMahon's Master Theorem $\det(I-XA)^{-1}$, symmetric function ring $\Lambda$ and Newton–Girard char-$p$ asymmetry, 2D quarter-plane Obstinate Kernel Method (dihedral group $\mathcal{G} = \langle \Phi, \Psi \rangle$), and bivariate PDE companion matrix products.
- [Checkpoint IV · Part IV Blind Assessment (`CP-IV`)](checkpoints/cp04-part4-pgf-walks-multivariate.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 17`.

### Part V · D-Finite Series, Differential Operators, Transposition & Fast Composition (`Ch 18`–`Ch 21`)

- [Ch 18 · D-Finite Series, Euler Operator $\vartheta$, 7 ODE Archetypes & $p$-Adic Indicial Lifting](chapters/ch18-d-finite-weyl-algebra-p-recursive-indicial-lifting.qmd): D-finite $\leftrightarrow$ P-recursive equivalence via $\vartheta = xD_x$, Abel–Cockle–Harley–Comtet algebraic-to-ODE conversion, the 7 ODE linearization archetypes (including Riccati and exponential gauge), and $p$-adic indicial lifting over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{V+1}\mathbb{Z}$.
- [Ch 19 · Shift Algebra, Creative Telescoping (WZ), Coupled Sparse Composition & Truncated Taylor ODEs](chapters/ch19-coupled-sparse-composition-wz-truncated-taylor-ode.qmd): Weyl algebra $K[x]\langle D_x \rangle$ and shift algebra $K[n]\langle E_n \rangle$, Zeilberger WZ pairs, `EI` direct differential-residue binomial sums, coupled $r$-state $O(rNK)$ sparse composition, and `EI 科技` $O(K)$ truncated Taylor ODEs.
- [Ch 20 · Tellegen's Transposition Principle, Middle Product `mulT`, Multipoint Evaluation & Sampling Shift](chapters/ch20-tellegen-transposition-multipoint-sampling-shift.qmd): DAG edge reversal $(E_k \cdots E_1)^\top$, DIF/DIT butterfly duality, middle product `mulT` ($1.5\,\mathcal{M}(N)$ Newton `inv`), division-free transposed multipoint `eval` and `interp`, transposed Chirp-Z ($\text{czt}^\top$), shift of sampling points (`连续点值平移`), and $O(\sqrt{P}\log P)$ block factorials.
- [Ch 21 · Power Projection, Kinoshita–Li $O(N \log^2 N)$ Composition & Dual-Route Compositional Inverse](chapters/ch21-kinoshita-li-composition-power-projection-revert.qmd): `power_projection` via Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori ($Q_r(0,y)=1$ zero-inversion invariant), `compose` as the exact Tellegen transpose of `power_projection`, Dual-Route `revert` (Route A for $p > N$, Route B Newton + `compose` for $p \le N$), and functional square roots $G(G(x)) = F(x)$ with the Artin–Schreier obstruction at degree $p+2$.
- [Checkpoint V · Part V Blind Assessment (`CP-V`)](checkpoints/cp05-part5-dfinite-transposition-composition.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 21`.

### Part VI · Tree-DP Accelerations, $q$-Analogues, Set Power Series & Dirichlet Rings (`Ch 22`–`Ch 24`)

- [Ch 22 · Polynomials on Trees: HLD Spine Divide-and-Conquer, Static Top Trees & Zero-Divisor Maintenance](chapters/ch22-tree-dp-fps-hld-static-top-tree-zero-divisor.qmd): subtree size-convolution bounds, HLD + weight-balanced static top tree (`全局平衡二叉树`) with min-heap `Rake` and 3-way weighted-midpoint `Compress`, Fourier-domain $3c^2$ matrix products, zero-divisor pairs $(a,c) \equiv a\cdot 0^c$, and rerooting Vandermonde `mulT`.
- [Ch 23 · $q$-Analogues, Gaussian Binomials, $q$-Difference Equations, $q$-Lucas & MacWilliams Duality](chapters/ch23-q-analogues-gaussian-binomials-q-lucas-macwilliams.qmd): $q$-Pochhammer $(a;q)_n$, Gaussian $q$-binomials $\binom{n}{k}_q$, Gauss/Cauchy $q$-binomial theorems, $q$-difference equations ($x \mapsto qx$), $q$-Lucas theorem when $\operatorname{ord}_p(q) \le n$, Durfee squares, Grassmannian subspace counting over $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and MacWilliams/Krawtchouk coding duality.
- [Ch 24 · Non-Cauchy Algebras: Bitwise FWT, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$ & Dirichlet Ring $\mathcal{D}_f$](chapters/ch24-bitwise-fwt-set-power-series-dirichlet_gf.qmd): OR/AND/XOR FWT, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n = K[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^2,\dots,x_n^2)$, L1-contiguous ranked FZT, division-free $O(n^2 2^n)$ SPS `inv`/`ln`/`exp` via MSB derivative $\partial/\partial x_v$, `Elegia` Taylor-shift SPS composition, pointed biconnected SPS $\ln$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$ with prime-multiplicity $\Omega(n)$-derivation $\vartheta$.
- [Checkpoint VI · Part VI Blind Assessment (`CP-VI`)](checkpoints/cp06-part6-trees-qseries-sps-dirichlet.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning the entire 24-chapter FPS curriculum.
